acceptance.item: P6-RT-09-01: Glossary rows 35 and 36 define 'highest root' and 'root poset' by facts of simply laced boards, false on B, C, F, G
acceptance.test: site/tests/unit/content-glossary-highest-root.test.ts > highest root: the definition names one root population on each of the 32 boards, and it is the highest root; > root poset: the definition is the order of the positive root populations, and its raising moves are its covers only with single roads
acceptance.evidence: Severity blocker (no adjustment). Red at base e76cd3d: 2 failed (2), same observed as the verifier (16 of 32 boards with two unraised roots; B2 raising moves (0,1)->(1,1), (1,0)->(1,2) against covers (0,1)->(1,1), (1,0)->(1,1), (1,1)->(1,2)). Cause: both definitions dropped M1's hypothesis 'a board of finite type with single roads'. Row 35 is now 'the root population of largest form value at which no mutation raises any city' (SPEC 2.6). Its data-claim says that with single roads it is the only one, that with a double or triple road there is exactly one other of smaller form value, the highest short root, and that Kostant's game, attributed to Kostant, ends there from a short simple root population (F13, T9). Row 36 is the order of the positive root populations, city by city; the raising-move picture is the root poset only with single roads (T2, 2.16). The test checks every statement on all 32 golden boards with the engine (roots, mutate, formValue, kostantPlay) against types.highest_root, highest_short_root and kostant.end_from_node. Green: 5 passed with glossary.test.ts; M10.spec 22 passed. Commit 63636c4.

acceptance.item: P6-RT-09-03: Glossary row 64 says the shape of a Wythoff polytope depends only on which nodes are ringed; SPEC says its combinatorics
acceptance.test: site/tests/unit/content-glossary-wythoff.test.ts > B3 (0,1,1) and (0,2,1): the same rings and face counts, edge lengths in the ratio 2 against 8
acceptance.evidence: Severity minor; fixed because the fixer was already in glossary.mdx. Red at base: 1 failed, f-vector (24, 36, 14) for both, squared edge lengths 2 and 4 against 2 and 16. Cause: 'shape' was used where SPEC 2.14 says combinatorics. The cited claim now reads 'Its faces, and the way they meet, depend only on which nodes are ringed (Cox35, CKPS95)', followed by 'The lengths of its edges depend on the rings too, so two orbits with the same ringed nodes can differ in shape.' The f-vectors now come from the engine's wythoffFVector and the lengths from its symmetrizer, beside the oracle's values. Green: 1 passed. Commit cf00a6a.
